status.line: Shows whether Hide is running, with its process, its port and how many clients are connected to it.

stop.line: Stops Hide's background service on this machine, so Hide is no longer running until you open it again.

version.line: Shows the version and commit of this Hide build.

guide.line: Prints the guide Hide gives an agent in its pane: letters, agents, the operator's screen and Project Memory.

issue help.line: Prints the steps for reporting a bug in Hide itself to its GitHub issues, which an agent follows once you agree.

contract.line: Prints the commands that tools call and the answers they get, as JSON, so a tool can check it matches this build.

request send.line: Sends a letter from an agent's pane to another agent and keeps its reply; sending again with the same --intent retries that letter without delivering it twice, and a new letter needs a new --intent.
request send.example: hide request send parent-name --kind progress --intent task-plan-1 --body 'Plan: core first, then web.'

request reply.line: Answers a letter you received, so the sender gets your answer with the letter it was about.
request reply.example: hide request reply letter-1 --intent task-answer-1 --body 'The check passed.'

request ack.line: Records, from the recipient's own pane, that it received a letter, which is the receipt the sender waits for.

request cancel.line: Cancels a letter you sent that is still waiting for its answer.

request show.line: Opens one letter in full, including a letter that an inbox bundle only lists by its id.

inbox.line: Lists the letters waiting for you and the ones that came back undelivered, with the command that marks them taken.

watch start.line: Starts a watch on an agent, so you get a letter when that agent has been quiet for too long or has stopped at a question or a prompt; the watch ends when the agent exits, reports that it is finished, or you stop it.

watch assign.line: Hands a watch to another observer, so its quiet-time letters go to the new one; the current observer can hand it over, and an observer can take it for itself by naming itself with --approval and the watch's current --expected-generation.

watch stop.line: Stops a watch, so its observer no longer gets letters about that agent.

watch list.line: Lists the watches that are running and who observes each one.

agent register.line: Adds an agent that you started yourself in a Hide pane to Hide's list of agents, with the parent you name if you name one.

agent list.line: Lists the agents Hide knows, with the machine each runs on and whether it is running, asleep or ended.

agent show.line: Shows one agent: its id, its parent, its machine, and what it is doing and waiting on now.

agent ask-human.line: Tells the operator that a step needs a person, such as a sign-in or a permission; you then end your turn and wait for the letter that says it is done.

agent end.line: Ends an agent and closes its pane, keeping its conversation so the operator can resume it; with --keep-pane only the agent's registration ends, and to end yourself you need --keep-pane, since otherwise your own pane closes before the command gets its answer.

agent sleep.line: Puts a child of yours (or yourself) to sleep, its process ending and its conversation kept, so a request or block letter wakes it again; it is refused while the agent works, waits for the operator or is on the operator's screen.

agent archive.line: Saves an agent's conversation and closes its panes, so the operator can resume it later from the archive; a session that is working is refused, and only the operator confirms that, on Hide's screen.

agent catalog.line: Lists the agent kinds and profiles Hide can start, with whether each is installed and the models and efforts each one takes.

agent profile list.line: Lists this machine's agent profiles, each one a way to start an agent, with its account, program, environment variable names and installation state.

agent profile add.line: Adds a profile for an agent kind, such as a second account with its own folder, that a start can then choose with --profile.
agent profile add.example: hide agent profile add claude work --account ~/.claude-work

agent profile edit.line: Changes a profile's name, program or environment variables; the built-in default profile cannot be edited.
agent profile edit.example: hide agent profile edit claude work --rename client

agent profile default.line: Makes a profile the one an agent starts with when nothing else chooses a profile.
agent profile default.example: hide agent profile default claude work

agent profile remove.line: Removes a profile that no running or sleeping agent uses; the built-in default profile cannot be removed.
agent profile remove.example: hide agent profile remove claude work

agent profile reinstall.line: Installs Hide's hooks into a profile's account folder again.
agent profile reinstall.example: hide agent profile reinstall claude work

agent spawn.line: Starts a new agent in a tab of its own, or beside your pane with --beside (your own checkout only), and gives it a brief to start on; --machine starts it on a device, and only the machine that runs Hide may do that.
agent spawn.example: hide agent spawn --parent here --name review-1 --intent review-1 --kind claude --repo ~/projects/app --branch review-1 --brief 'Review the diff and report.'

ps.line: Shows the panes and agents Hide runs, as a tree of checkouts, tabs and panes; --here keeps only this project.

device list.line: Lists the devices connected to this Hide, with each one's state and whatever it is waiting on from you; run it on the machine that runs Hide, since a device is refused.

device add.line: Registers a computer you reach over SSH, by its Host name in ~/.ssh/config, as a device; its folders, Git and terminals wait until the operator chooses Allow and install on its row in Settings > Devices. Only the machine that runs Hide may add one.

device remove.line: Forgets a device, and takes Hide's helper off it only if the helper is connected at that moment and no other registered device reaches the same account there; otherwise the helper stays and the reason goes to Hide's diagnostics. Its panes and agents keep running there.

device retry.line: Starts a new attempt to connect a device, which may ask the operator; a device that is connected, connecting or waiting on the operator gets no new attempt, and only the machine that runs Hide may ask. With --wait it waits until the device connects, needs the operator, the attempt fails or five minutes pass.

mission help.line: Prints the guide for a mission's Conductor, the agent that plans a mission and starts the agents that do its work.

mission create.line: Creates a new mission with a title, which a plan and its agents then carry out.
mission create.example: hide mission create --title 'Fix the lens filter'

mission plan.line: Sets a mission's plan from a JSON file: its nodes, their order, their checks and the worker for each.

mission node.line: Updates one node of a mission's plan, such as its status, its branch, its pull request or its worker.
mission node.example: hide mission node fix-1487 --status working --agent-id agent-7

mission record.line: Records one finish line of a node as passed or failed, with the evidence that shows it.
mission record.example: hide mission record fix-1487 c1 --pass --evidence 'The lens keeps its filter after a reload.'

mission skip.line: Marks one finish line of a node as skipped, with a reason, so the node can go on.
mission skip.example: hide mission skip cause c2 --reason 'Covered by the next node.'

mission defect.line: Reopens an earlier node with a defect that a later node found, so its worker can fix it.
mission defect.example: hide mission defect fix-1487 --found-by together --line 'The lens loses its filter after a reload.'

mission gate.line: Settles a place the operator asked to check, using the operator's own words, so the node can finish.

mission start.line: Moves a planned mission from Planning to Running once the operator has approved its plan; the Conductor then starts the workers.

mission decide.line: Puts a question for the operator on the mission's map, or clears it with --clear once it is answered.
mission decide.example: hide mission decide --line 'Ship the lens fix in this pull request?' --option yes --option no

mission delay.line: Records why new starts are held for a mission, such as usage near a limit; holding them is the Conductor's job, and --clear removes the reason.
mission delay.example: hide mission delay --line 'Usage is close to the limit.'

mission close.line: Closes a mission as done, as waiting for merge, or as cancelled, with a report of what it did.

mission reopen.line: Opens a mission that was closed as done or as waiting for merge again, so its nodes can continue; a cancelled mission cannot be reopened.

mission take.line: Takes over a mission whose Conductor is gone, so you become the one that runs its plan.

mission show.line: Shows a mission as text, or one node in full, or the whole record as JSON with --json.

mission list.line: Lists the missions in this Hide, with their status and their Conductor.

mission settings.line: Shows the mission defaults: how many agents may run at once, the default scope and the worker candidates.

task help.line: Prints the guide for keeping your own plan of steps, which Hide shows as a map beside your pane.

task set.line: Puts up the steps of your task, so the operator can see where you are on the map beside your pane.

task node.line: Changes one step of your plan: its status, a line about it, or the pull request or file that finishes it.
task node.example: hide task node spec --status done --file docs/spec.md

task approve.line: Records that the operator approved the plan you put up for review, so your writes, commits and pushes are allowed again.

task drop.line: Drops a plan the operator asked you not to carry out.

task show.line: Shows an agent's plan, with the status of each of its steps.

pane read.line: Prints the last lines of a pane, unwrapped, so you can see what its program last showed.

pane send.line: Types text into a pane, or presses keys in it such as Escape or Enter; it is refused while the pane's input box holds a draft that someone typed there, and it is input, not a letter, so nothing keeps a reply or retries it.

pane open.line: Opens a new pane beside your own pane, in your checkout, and runs a command in it, without moving your keyboard focus unless you add --focus.
pane open.example: hide pane open --beside -- npm run dev

agent read.line: Prints the last lines of an agent's pane, so you can see what the agent last showed.

workspace purpose.line: Sets the one-line purpose of your checkout, which the sidebar shows; it can be 40 characters at most.
workspace purpose.example: hide workspace purpose 'Fix the lens filter'

workspace info.line: Shows the workspace and checkout Hide has for this folder, and the device they run on.

file open.line: Shows a file to the operator in Hide's View as a tab, where it waits until they look at it; it needs Hide's window open, and while the operator is looking at another pane of your checkout, the file waits in your session's Files list instead of taking the screen.

diff open.line: Shows the changes to a file to the operator in Hide's View as a tab, where it waits until they look at it; it needs Hide's window open, and while the operator is looking at another pane of your checkout, it waits in your session's Files list instead of taking the screen.

browser open.line: Opens a web page, or a local file, as a browser tab in Hide's View, where it waits until the operator looks at it; it needs Hide's window open, and while the operator is looking at another pane of your checkout, the tab waits behind what they see. Only an http(s) or blank page can be driven by the other browser commands.

browser connect.line: Asks Hide for the browser display of this checkout, or the one you name with --display, and prints its answer.

browser snapshot.line: Reads the page in one of your own checkout's browser displays as a list of its elements, each with a ref you can act on; it also works while the display is behind another tab of its area.

browser click.line: Clicks an element of the page, by its ref, by its visible text, or by a point, only while its View is the selected one of its area; behind another tab it fails with display_hidden.

browser fill.line: Fills a form field of the page with a value.

browser type.line: Types text into the page, only while its View is the selected one of its area; behind another tab it fails with display_hidden.

browser press.line: Presses a key in the page, such as Enter, Tab or Escape, only while its View is the selected one of its area; behind another tab it fails with display_hidden.

browser hover.line: Moves the pointer over an element of the page, so a menu or tooltip can show, only while its View is the selected one of its area; behind another tab it fails with display_hidden.

browser drag.line: Drags from one element or point of the page to another, only while its View is the selected one of its area; behind another tab it fails with display_hidden.

browser scroll.line: Scrolls the page up or down, or to an element.

browser wait.line: Waits until a text or an element appears in the page; with --gone and a selector it waits until that element disappears instead. It stops at a timeout.

browser screenshot.line: Saves a picture of the page, or of one element with --ref, to a file, only while its View is the selected one of its area; behind another tab it fails with display_hidden.

browser eval.line: Runs a JavaScript expression in the page and prints its result.

browser console.line: Shows the messages the page logged to its console, newest first.

browser network.line: Shows the network requests the page made, with their timing but not their headers or bodies.

browser help.line: Prints the guide for driving a browser display: its refs, how actions are checked, and what each failure means.

view list.line: Lists the Views open in your checkout, with the ids that the other view and browser commands take.

view status.line: Shows one View by its id, so you can read what a delegated agent opened in it.

view select.line: Brings a View to the front of its area when the operator is looking at your pane. If they are looking at another pane of the same checkout, the command succeeds but their selection stays as it was.

view close.line: Closes a View, so it leaves the operator's screen; the last View of a document with an unsaved draft is refused until the operator saves or discards the draft in Hide.

view split.line: Moves a View into a new area on one edge of the area you name, so it sits beside the others; the result may not have more than six areas or three levels of splits, and a View alone in its area cannot be split off from that same area.
view split.example: hide view split browser-3 --area area-1 --edge right

view move.line: Moves a View into another area, at the position you give.

links pr.line: Shows the projects and sessions Hide has linked to a pull request.

links issue.line: Shows the sessions and pull requests Hide has linked to a GitHub issue in this project.

links branch.line: Shows the pull requests and sessions Hide has linked to a Git branch in this project.

links session.line: Shows the named session and the pull requests tied to it.

session list.line: Lists the recent sessions of this project, one line each with a summary, and, when Hide knows this project's repository, those of the projects of the same repository on connected devices.

session record.line: Shows one session as its record: its summary, its state and the requests it received.

session read.line: Reads the raw events of a session around one request, for when the exact words or tool output matter.

memory show.line: Prints one Project Memory card in full, with its status and where its words came from.

memory search.line: Finds Project Memory cards that match some words, and prints each card's number and title.

memory add.line: Sends a decision the operator made to Project Memory, which writes it as a card that later agents can read.
memory add.example: hide memory add 'Use the staging database for migration tests.'

memory forget.line: Takes a Project Memory card out of use, when the operator asks for it; memory undo brings it back.

memory undo.line: Brings back a Project Memory card that was taken out of use.

memory placed.line: Records that a Project Memory card has been written into a document at a path, for the agent that moves cards into documents.

memory building.line: Records the branch that implements a Project Memory card's decision and the file there that already documents it, for the agent that moves cards into documents.

memory unbuilt.line: Records why a Project Memory card cannot be written into a document yet, for the agent that moves cards into documents.

memory outdated.line: Records why a Project Memory card is outdated and marks it for another check, for the agent that moves cards into documents.

memory skipped.line: Records why a Project Memory card was skipped when moving cards into documents.

memory stale.line: Reports that a Project Memory card no longer matches what the operator said, so Hide holds it back from agents until the session is analyzed, the hold is released or its time runs out; a hold is only accepted for a card whose full text this session's prompt gave the agent, not for one it only looked up with memory show or saw in the starting list.
memory stale.example: hide memory stale m508 'The operator moved the issue template.'

memory release.line: Ends a hold that an agent's stale report put on a card, so agents get the card again.

memory recheck.line: Asks for a Project Memory card to be checked again, and keeps it out of agents' prompts until that check ends; it needs Hide AI on, and an agent may ask only for a card its prompt gave it (the starting list counts, memory show alone does not).
